title: Always in need of renewal
hook: Vatican II says Christ calls the Church to continual reformation (Unitatis Redintegratio 6)

segments.voice: Yesterday, Paul of the Cross, preaching the crucifix through his own long darkness. Your line was remember the passion. Did you pause at a cross? Today we close a whole stretch of the long story: reform, mission and revolution. Day eight hundred eighty-six.

Scaffolding climbs one tower of an old cathedral while Mass goes on inside. Stonemasons up top, replacing what the weather wore away; a choir below, singing what it has sung for generations. The scaffolding doesn't mean the building is false. It means the building is still in use. At the Second Vatican Council, the bishops wrote a sentence about the Church that sounds like that scaffolding. It's in a document on Christian unity, and it says the Church is always being called to renewal.
screen: `SCAFFOLDING ON THE TOWER.` → `MASS GOES ON INSIDE.` → `A SENTENCE FROM THE COUNCIL.`

segments.voice: In paraphrase, the sentence says this: Christ calls the Church, still on her journey, to keep reforming, and she always needs it, because she is also a human institution on earth. Take it a piece at a time. First, who calls. The council doesn't say reform is a good idea people had. It says the call comes from Christ. Second, what needs renewing. The same passage names failings in conduct, in church discipline, even in the way teaching has been worded, and says these should be set right, while keeping distinct the faith itself, which it does not treat as up for change. Third, the road we've just walked held both. A wounded soldier praying in Manresa, Teresa on the road, Vincent de Paul and the poor, Kongo's king, Mother Seton's schools, the hidden families of Japan. And Galileo, the slave trade, the pain of the California missions, the Jesuits suppressed. Renewal and failure, side by side, in the same Church. Fourth, the person. Catholic teaching speaks of conversion not as something done once, but as a lifelong task for every baptized person. What is true of the Church is true of each member. In the Apocalypse, also called Revelation, in the Douay-Rheims, the one on the throne says: "Behold, I make all things new." Not once and finished. Being made new.
screen: `THE CALL COMES FROM CHRIST.` · `CONDUCT, DISCIPLINE, WORDING.` · `RENEWAL AND FAILURE, SIDE BY SIDE.` · `CONVERSION IS A LIFELONG TASK.` · then, large: `BEHOLD, I MAKE ALL THINGS NEW.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: renew one thing in yourself. Settle, and breathe. Think of one habit, one relationship, one corner of your life that has worn down, the way stone wears in weather. Not everything. One thing. Don't tear it down in your head. Just ask what small repair would look like this week. An apology. A return to something you dropped. A kinder way of speaking. If you pray, you can ask God for help with it. If you don't, simply hold it honestly. The bell holds the time.
Always in need of renewal. The council's teaching that Christ keeps calling the Church, and every member of it, to be made new.
screen: `ALWAYS IN NEED OF RENEWAL — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: always renewing. Today, make the one small repair you chose. Tomorrow, the modern Church begins, with a struggling parish priest in a French village. Day eight hundred eighty-six.

howItsDone: Catholics speak of continual conversion, renewed through confession, Lent and retreats, and parishes and dioceses hold synods and renewal programs to examine how they live the faith.

fork.setup: you're one of the bishops at the council, writing about the Church. do you say she needs reform?
options: no. say the Church has never needed fixing.
yes. say Christ calls her to continual reformation.
fork.reveal: the council wrote, in effect, that Christ calls the Church on her journey to keep reforming, which she always needs because she is also a human institution.

original.note: Latin: continual reformation, the council's phrase (as perennem reformationem) in Unitatis Redintegratio 6.

trapdoor: what you thought: reform is something a church does once, after a scandal.
what it means: the council says Christ calls the Church to continual renewal, and each member to lifelong conversion.
what a scholar hears: Unitatis Redintegratio 6 names conduct, discipline and the wording of teaching as open to correction, distinct from the faith itself.
